subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support Slack user-level Events API routing and replies as a regular Slack user identity, and if so what opt-in authorization/audit boundary is required?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior lets OpenClaw receive and speak as a human Slack account without the normal app identity marker, which is a product and security trust-boundary choice.

options.title: Design explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add an opt-in Slack plugin mode with scoped xoxp authorization matching, send-token selection, allowlist/pairing checks, docs, and live proof before enabling it.

options.title: Keep bot-only ingress documented
options.body: Close this product direction by documenting that user-level Slack event subscriptions are unsupported and users should DM the Slack app/bot identity instead.

options.title: Prototype outside bundled Slack first
options.body: Ask for an external plugin or fork proof that demonstrates the user-token event and reply model before deciding whether to promote it into bundled Slack.

recommendation.title: Design explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in Slack plugin mode with scoped xoxp authorization matching, send-token selection, allowlist/pairing checks, docs, and live proof before enabling it.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible recent history across Slack identity, send, Socket Mode, docs, and review decisions for this boundary.
